basis: Tumor arises in spinal nerve roots; sensory loss, weakness and cord compression remain within the neurologic axis.
Spigelian hernia is an abdominal wall fascial defect; cryptorchidism is reproductive and outside the axes. Herniation alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Primary microcephaly and developmental impairment define it; short fingers and clinodactyly each occur in 2/5. Constipation alone does not establish bowel damage.
Myelodysplasia, immunodeficiency and psychomotor developmental delay are defining features. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease.
Benign tumor of small dermal blood vessels; both cutaneous location and vascular origin define the lesion.
Skeletal dysplasia with epiphyseal and vertebral abnormalities; laryngeal stenosis occurs in 1/3, supporting airway involvement. Stridor occurs in 2/3.
Defining abnormalities include vertebral and rib dysostosis, arthrogryposis, pulmonary hypoplasia and multiple cutaneous pterygia.
Astrocytic neurodegeneration; structural scoliosis is reported in 80-99%. Eye movement and bulbar abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Inborn immune disorder defined by inflammatory bowel disease and recurrent infections of the sinuses and lungs.
Isolated autosomal recessive hearing loss; no syndromic organ involvement established.
Ataxia from dysfunction of sensory pathways. Vestibular disease is a subtype and does not establish ear involvement across the umbrella.
Disease of dental pulp; teeth and oral tissues belong to the gastrointestinal axis. Infection is not shared by all subtypes.
Fluid accumulation around the testis is a male reproductive disorder, without intrinsic involvement of the listed axes.
Radioulnar synostosis and thrombocytopenia define it; sensorineural deafness occurs in 2/3 and intellectual disability in 1/3. Cleft palate in 1/3 omitted by cap.
Nonsyndromic profound sensorineural hearing loss in 8/8; motor delay in 2/8 is below the involvement threshold.
Autoimmune cutaneous melanocyte loss produces depigmented skin with an intermediate inflammatory tan zone.
Metabolic epileptic encephalopathy with deficient cerebral folate availability. Respiratory distress and abdominal distention do not establish direct organ damage.
Hypocellular marrow failure causes cytopenias; most cases are acquired and immune-mediated, although inherited and toxic forms also occur.
Bone fragility and recurrent fractures define WNT1 osteogenesis imperfecta. Blue sclerae are non-damaging; developmental delay occurs in only 1/9.
Catecholamine-secreting paraganglionic neuroendocrine tumor. Hypertension is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than an additional organ label.
Scalp aplasia and limb reduction define it; hydrocephalus, seizures and severe developmental delay occur in 1/2. Optic atrophy is 3/12; other eye lesions are occasional.
Mitochondrial complex III metabolic disorder with defining renal tubulopathy and liver failure; encephalopathy is a defining manifestation of the syndrome.
Mucinous epithelial carcinoma of the exocrine pancreas; no common direct involvement of another axis is established.
Paralysis of the ocular ciliary muscle causes loss of accommodation; no separate neurologic lesion is implied.
Cleft lip is an oral structural malformation; progressive retinal degeneration is the other defining feature.
